title: Uptober Expectations Futile: But the Numbers Tell a Different Story for Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH)! Santiment Reveals!
body: October, the historic month of rebound that cryptocurrency investors had been anticipating after major declines, ended in great disappointment. Bitcoin closed October, known as Uptober (the month of price increases), with a drop of approximately 7 percent. However, Santiment noted that this did not mean Bitcoin had given up. “No Uptober, No Bitcoin Surrender” Cryptocurrency analysis platform Santiment has published its Bitcoin report for October. It stated that the expected rise in the crypto market did not materialize and that “Uptober” never arrived. However, Santiment noted that investors maintained their profitable positions despite the price drop. “…Following Bitcoin’s strong recovery in August and September, the outlook looked very favorable for October as well. However, instead, BTC spent October struggling to maintain its gains, most altcoins performed significantly worse, AI enthusiasm waned, memecoins lost value, security concerns increased, and the month ended with a multi-billion dollar Binance hack casting a shadow over the market.” Major Bitcoin Wallets Continue to Accumulate! According to Santiment data, despite the price drop, whale wallets holding between 10 and 10,000 BTC accumulated approximately 91,500 BTC between September 18 and October 31. The total Bitcoin holdings in these wallets have risen to 13.69 million BTC, reaching 68.1% of the circulating supply. Santiment noted that this group includes exchanges and custodians, therefore the entire accumulation cannot be interpreted as purchases by individual investors. Santiment added that although BTC closed the month lower, BTC investors still made a net profit of approximately $7.86 billion. Binance Attack Became the Biggest Hack in Crypto History! As October drew to a close, the cryptocurrency market was shaken by the largest cyberattack in its history. The Binance hack, which resulted in the theft of $6.3 billion in assets, surpassed the Bybit attack, which recorded losses of $1.5 billion. “…Following the news of the Binance hack, Bitcoin dropped below $80,000 and eventually fell as low as $76,500.” Santiment noted that the Binance hack was the focus of the market for days, and that the number of posts related to the hack rose to 2,995 on October 30th. This figure was approximately double the peak of 1,532 during the Bybit attack. Ethereum Diverges from Bitcoin! Santiment reported that, unlike Bitcoin investors, Ethereum investors experienced a net realized loss of approximately $510 million in October. According to Santiment data, 16 out of the 18 days between October 14th and 31st resulted in losses. Santiment noted that a record-breaking hack in October saw Bitcoin sentiment hit a three-month low, but Bitcoin investors still hadn’t given up. *This is not investment advice. title: Reap, Meitu’s EveLab Insight, and Pivota Sign MOU to Explore Bringing Agentic Beauty Shopping to Life
tags: Press Release|Agentic Commerce|agentic payments|AI beauty shopping|AI checkout|AI shopping|EveLab Insight|MakeupPlus|Meitu|personalized commerce|Pivota|Reap|stablecoin payments
body: BitcoinWorld Reap, Meitu’s EveLab Insight, and Pivota Sign MOU to Explore Bringing Agentic Beauty Shopping to Life The collaboration would connect personalized consumer experiences and the checkout experience with Reap’s agentic payments solution HONG KONG , Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Reap , a global financial technology company that enables financial connectivity and access for businesses worldwide through stablecoin-enabled infrastructure, has recently signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to explore a strategic collaboration with Meitu’s EveLab Insight, a provider of international skin analysis solutions and publisher of the MakeupPlus app, and also Pivota, a global commerce technology company that connects AI applications with merchants and payment infrastructure. The collaboration aims to bring personalized, AI-assisted shopping experiences to beauty consumers, helping them move seamlessly from product discovery towards merchant checkout and payment. A shopper could get a skin and beauty analysis through MakeupPlus, and with the shopper’s consent and based on their preferences, receive relevant recommendations. Pivota would assess suitable products, merchants and purchase channels, taking into account factors such as price and availability, then Reap would handle the checkout and order confirmation through supported integrations. The shopper would remain in control of the purchase, and where required, review the payment details and approve it via a secure passkey. Reap’s agentic payments service is designed to support agent-initiated card payments under user-approved mandates with payment credentials, spending controls and transaction records. “AI is getting very good at helping people find what they want. Paying for it is still where the experience breaks down,” said Daren Guo, Co-Founder, Reap . “Reap’s agentic payments are built to close that gap, and they’re part of our vision to reimagine how people pay. We want to make the last step simple and safe, so an agent can complete the purchase within parameters approved by the consumer. With EveLab Insight, we want to show how AI-led discovery and payments technology can come together in one seamless shopping experience.” “We’re excited about the opportunity to explore potential practical use cases that could demonstrate how AI can make beauty discovery more personal and useful. Personalization should help people discover products that feel right for them, including things they may not have thought to search for,” said Zha Xi, CEO, EveLab Insight . “Beauty is especially suited to this because individual preferences matter so much. Exploring how AI-led discovery can connect with a smoother path to purchase could make the experience feel more relevant and useful to shoppers.” “A good shopping experience is not just about finding relevant products; it is about helping customers act on that recommendation when they are ready to buy. Pivota helps evaluate the relevant products, merchants and purchase channels based on factors such as availability, price and transaction feasibility. Together with EveLab Insight and Reap, we are exploring how that can make personalised beauty shopping more seamless, while leaving the customer in control of the purchase,” said Peng Xu, Founder and CEO at Pivota . Beauty shopping can inspire a purchase long before a shopper knows exactly what to look for. This collaboration aims to enhance the shopping experience by connecting EveLab Insight’s personalized recommendations to Pivota’s product and merchant capabilities, then carrying the shopper’s choice through Reap’s payment infrastructure with their approval. If deployed, consumers could discover products they might otherwise miss, while partners could gain a practical way to bring agentic commerce from recommendation to checkout. About EveLab Insight EveLab Insight provides AI skin analysis, high-resolution imaging and beauty-tech solutions for spas and global skincare brands. Developed and published by EveLab Insight, MakeupPlus is an AI-powered portrait makeup camera and photo-touchup app for iOS and Android. It enables users to try on makeup virtually using real-time AR, alongside tools for skin and facial-feature retouching. About Pivota Pivota is building the commerce decision and execution layer for AI agents, connecting AI-powered applications with merchants and payment infrastructure to turn product discovery into real transactions. Its platform enables intelligent product and merchant selection, acceptance intelligence, checkout and payment routing, and order execution through integrated partners. Pivota does not hold or transfer customer funds or provide financing. About Reap Reap is a global financial technology company that enables financial connectivity and access for businesses worldwide through stablecoin-native infrastructure. Our mission is to transform the financial landscape into a more interconnected space for efficient money movement by merging traditional finance with digital assets, bridging disparate economies and connecting key financial markets. Reap was an early leader in Asia to incorporate stablecoins into our solutions and now processes billions in stablecoin-funded transaction flows, reflecting the rapid adoption of stablecoins by businesses globally. From stablecoin-enabled corporate cards to cross-border payments, we streamline financial operations and empower companies to scale with our integrated business accounts and embedded finance solutions. In 2026, Reap was acquired by Payward, the parent of Kraken, in one of Asia’s largest fintech exits, joining one interoperable stack spanning trading, custody, payments, lending, onchain finance, and benchmarks. Founded in 2018 in Hong Kong, Reap now employs 300 people worldwide. More information about Reap can be found at reap.global . title: Nvidia-backed Agility goes public, becomes America’s first humanoid robot stock
body: The Nvidia-backed humanoid robot maker, Agility Robotics (NASDAQ: AGLT), will make its trading debut on the Nasdaq when markets open November 5. The market debut, arranged via a $465 million SPAC merger, means the United States finally has a publicly traded company with humanoid robots as its core business. The milestone moment arrives roughly three months after Unitree went public in China at an almost 20x valuation of the US humanoid robots maker. How Agility went public Agility’s first trading day arrives via a reverse merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI, a special purpose acquisition company run by financier Michael Klein. Pre-money equity was set at $2.5 billion. The combined company will trade under the AGLT and AGLTW tickers , as Churchill XI moved on from their old symbols upon the deal closing. The $465 million in gross capital before expenses the transaction and related financings brought in breaks down as: $164 million from the SPAC trust $201 million from a Foxconn-led private placement $100 million raised earlier No insiders sold on the way in, as existing shareholders’ equity was rolled into the new entity. Agility is backed by Nvidia, Amazon and SoftBank. The humanoid robotics company plans to use Nvidia’s IGX Thor platform to standardize its next robot’s onboard computing. Foxconn’s $201 million commitment also signals the level of stakes the one of the world’s largest contract manufacturers has in the firm. Comparing Agility to Unitree Unitree was worth roughly $50 billion at the end of the morning session of its first trading day on Shanghai’s STAR Market in August. That valuation was driven by a 629% price surge on that first day. The Hangzhou-based Unitree went public as an already profitable robot maker backed by Alibaba, DeepSeek and Tencent. Agility, on the other hand, reported $1.8 million in 2025 revenue and estimates this year’s operating loss between $138 million and $140 million. However, the company is drawing optimism from its order book. Its flagship Digit robot has logged more than 65,000 operating hours at customers including GXO, Schaeffler, Toyota and Amazon. Agility said the next-generation Digit 5, unveiled in September, holds over $300 million in committed multi-year orders. The latter depends on contractual milestones and product specifications. CEO Peggy Johnson, a former Magic Leap, Microsoft and Qualcomm executive, framed the listing around factory floors rather than markets. “Today marks an important milestone for Agility, but the bigger story is what it means for the future of work,” she said in the company’s statement. Agility intends to spend the new capital scaling production at RoboFab, its 70,000-square-foot Salem plant designed for up to 10,000 robots a year. title: Bitcoin Price Analysis: $80K Battle Rages On as BTC’s Next Targets Come Into Focus
body: Bitcoin is trading around $79.7K after a sharp rebound from the $75K region stalled near $80K. The rejection keeps BTC within a short-term corrective structure, with the price now caught between a key demand zone below and overhead resistance that buyers have repeatedly failed to clear. Meanwhile, the Adjusted SOPR is sliding back toward its key 1 threshold, suggesting that profit realization across the network is fading. Bitcoin Price Analysis: The Daily Chart Bitcoin continues to trade within the ascending channel that has defined its recovery from the June lows near $58K. However, after two rejections from the channel’s upper boundary around $87K in September and early October, BTC began forming lower highs and slipped below the channel’s midpoint late last month. The decline brought the price into the $75K-$78K demand zone, the order block that preceded the September rally toward $87K. Buyers responded with a long lower wick and a strong rebound, but the move stalled at the channel midline, which is now acting as resistance around $80K. Reclaiming it could pave the way for another advance toward the $87K supply zone, where the massive breakdown originated early this year. Conversely, a decisive daily close below $75K would invalidate the order block and leave the channel’s lower boundary near $73K as the next support. A breakdown beneath this trendline would mark a clear failure of the broader recovery structure and raise the risk of a deeper move toward the low $60K region, where the price consolidated during the summer. BTC/USDT 4-Hour Chart The 4-hour chart shows that BTC has been trading within a descending channel since the late-September highs near $87K, printing consistent lower highs and lower lows. The upper boundary has capped every notable rebound, including the October spike into the $85K supply zone, which sellers quickly absorbed. Yesterday, Bitcoin rallied aggressively from the $76K demand zone, which overlaps with the channel’s lower boundary. The move, however, was rejected at the confluence of the upper trendline and the $80K supply zone, which represents the bearish order block where the late-October breakdown began, and the price is now slipping back below it. A sustained break above this confluence would mark the first breakout from the channel and could open the way toward $85K, followed by the $87K highs. Until then, rebounds remain vulnerable to overhead supply. A renewed drop below $76K would leave the descending lower boundary near $75K as the final short-term support before the daily channel floor around $73K. On-Chain Analysis The Adjusted Spent Output Profit Ratio (aSOPR) on CryptoQuant measures whether coins moved on-chain are, on average, being spent at a profit or a loss, excluding outputs younger than one hour to filter out short-term noise. Readings above 1 indicate profit realization, while values below 1 suggest holders are selling at a loss. The chart displays the metric’s 30-day exponential moving average. The indicator remained above 1 throughout the 2024–2025 uptrend before dropping below it in early 2026, bottoming near 0.98 as BTC fell toward $60K. It reclaimed the threshold in August alongside the rally, peaking around 1.013 in October, but has since declined sharply toward approximately 1.003. In healthy uptrends, the 1 level tends to act as support, as holders are reluctant to sell at a loss. A rebound from here would suggest demand is absorbing supply around the $78K zone, while a sustained drop below it would point to loss-driven selling. The metric alone does not confirm direction, but a move beneath 1 alongside a daily close below $75K would considerably strengthen the bearish case and potentially lead to another round of capitulation. title: Tokenisation, Bitcoin and The Future of Capital Markets
body: From yield-bearing collateral to bitcoin-backed credit, the inaugural edition of The Future of Capital Markets explored how bitcoin and tokenised assets are evolving into the foundations of a more efficient, accessible and interconnected global financial system. Bitfinex Securities Head of Operations, Jesse Knutson moderates the discussion on bitcoin treasury companies . The tokenised asset market has grown into a multibillion-dollar industry over the past decade, attracting some of the world’s largest financial institutions. Yet compared with the scale of global capital markets, it still barely registers. Speaking at the inaugural edition of The Future of Capital Markets in Lugano, Switzerland, on 22 October, Adam Lawrence, co-founder and CEO of RWA.xyz , estimated the current value of tokenised assets on-chain at between $30 billion and $40 billion. In the context of global finance, he observed, that figure “effectively rounds to zero”. The observation captured both the scale of the opportunity and a central theme running through the day: the next phase of tokenised capital markets will be determined less by the number of assets tokenised than by the economic value they can deliver. Co-hosted by Bitfinex Securities and Blockstream Capital Partners , the event brought together asset managers, bitcoin treasury companies, financial institutions, regulators and infrastructure providers from around the world. Across ten panels, the conversation moved from the practical uses of tokenisation to the growing range of investment and financing structures being built around bitcoin as it becomes increasingly embedded in global finance. Tokenisation has to do more than represent an asset RWA.xyz’s data shows where tokenised capital is currently concentrated. US Treasuries lead the market, followed by private credit, while equities have only recently emerged as a significant category. Lawrence distinguished between assets distributed on-chain and those merely represented there. Regulated securities may still depend on an issuer, offering documents or an official investor register. The practical question is what investors can do with the token. Jesse Knutson, Head of Operations at Bitfinex Securities, emphasised self-custody as an important part of that test. “I think you should be able to withdraw it,” he said. “You should be able to self-custody it. And if you can’t do those things, is it tokenisation?” Greater control does not mean unrestricted transfer. Will Turner of Winston Taylor highlighted how whitelisting can allow investors to hold regulated securities in their own wallets while limiting transfers to verified participants. Technology cannot, however, create demand for an unattractive underlying investment. As Archax CEO and co-founder Graham Rodford put it: “Tokenising something doesn’t make it a good product.” Nor does continuous trading guarantee liquidity . Martin Baumann, co-founder and managing partner of CMCC Global , identified access, distribution and liquidity as tokenisation’s principal benefits. He pointed to the CREST and Liberty Bitcoin Accumulation (LBAF) funds as examples of a new distribution channel offering eligible investors smaller commitments and access to secondary trading. The regulatory discussion considered the environments in El Salvador and the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC), where Bitfinex Securities operates. Giles Dixon, Head of Global Regulatory Affairs at Bitfinex and Tether, argued that effective rules should focus on risks and outcomes, while giving issuers a route beyond experiments and sandboxes. The strongest case for tokenisation therefore lies not in putting an existing product on a blockchain for its own sake, but in improving how worthwhile investments are issued, distributed, held and transferred. Yield-bearing collateral is the use case One of the clearest use case examples of tokenisation is yield-bearing collateral. Trading firms routinely post assets as margin against derivatives positions, often using stablecoins that generate no return for the trader. Tokenised money-market funds offer an alternative : collateral that can continue earning income while supporting trading activity. Adam Back discusses tokenised fixed income and collateral. Rafael Mastroberardino of Franklin Templeton provided a live example, highlighting the hedge funds and market makers currently using interests in its Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund , available through the Benji platform , as collateral for trading positions. The assets can remain with a custodian and continue earning money-market yield rather than being transferred to an exchange as non-yielding margin. Blockstream co-founder and CEO Dr. Adam Back explained why that model could be particularly valuable in derivatives markets. Bitcoin traders may have little interest in money-market funds as standalone investments, he observed, but they already commit substantial collateral to perpetual-futures venues. Yield-bearing instruments could therefore lower the cost of maintaining those positions. As Lawrence put it, “Finance is about financing.” A token’s value increasingly depends on what its holder can do with it next. New financial structures developing around bitcoin Beyond tokenisation, The Future of Capital Markets also examined how bitcoin treasury companies, income-producing securities and collateralised lending are creating new routes to institutional participation. Tokenisation Around the World panel. Issuing equity at a premium to net asset value to buy bitcoin becomes less effective when that premium narrows or disappears. That has encouraged treasury companies to explore buybacks, acquisitions and preferred shares . Strive CEO Matt Cole said the notional amount outstanding of the company’s SATA preferred shares had grown from $200 million at launch to more than $1.4 billion in under a year. Discussing institutional demand for Strive’s preferred securities more broadly, Cole said investors showed little interest in potential bitcoin upside: “They just wanted the yield.” Sean Bill, co-founder and former chief strategy officer of BSTR, recalled that one public pension took two years to progress from its introduction to bitcoin to a small investment. In a separate panel, Bill said one idea discussed with pension funds was to invest in digital credit and use the income generated to build bitcoin exposure gradually, an approach that, he said, received “a pretty warm reception”. Bitcoin-backed lending presents a different opportunity, but one still shaped by the past failures of companies such as Celsius, BlockFi and other crypto lenders in 2022. Speakers identified maturity mismatches, undisclosed rehypothecation and undercollateralised lending as central weaknesses in the previous cycle. Newer models emphasise segregated collateral, transparent terms and restrictions on rehypothecation. Securitisation could eventually allow pensions and insurers to finance diversified pools of bitcoin-backed loans without originating individual loans. Institutional adoption will depend on how those safeguards perform under stress. What comes next Discussions at The Future of Capital Markets pointed to an industry increasingly focused on practical outcomes, namely better distribution, greater investor access and control, yield-bearing collateral and bitcoin financing structures suited to a wider range of mandates. Turning these opportunities into wider adoption will require genuine demand and useful secondary markets for tokenised funds. Collateral must remain legally enforceable and accessible when needed. bitcoin-based financing structures must meanwhile demonstrate that their economics are sustainable. Lawrence’s estimate shows how early the market remains. Progress will ultimately be measured not simply by the value of assets brought on-chain, but by whether those assets can move beyond their original point of issuance and be put to productive use. For Bitfinex Securities and the wider industry, the ultimate opportunity lies in making capital more accessible, transferable and useful to the investors who hold it. title: Elon Musk’s AI Predicts What XRP Price Will Be On November 30
body: Ripple’s annual Swell conference brought a wave of institutional announcements in late October 2026, from BNY Mellon custody support to expanded Robinhood integration of RLUSD settlement on the XRP Ledger. With that backdrop in place, XRP is trading at $1.27 as of early November, much lower than many expected. Market participants are curious about the asset’s future, wondering if it can meet expectations by the end of Monday. To explore that, we asked Grok, the AI assistant built by Elon Musk’s xAI, to project where XRP would stand by November 30. The Price Window for XRP Grok identified a general price window of $1.25 to $1.40 as the most probable range, with the central tendency sitting between $1.28 and $1.35. The AI characterized the outlook as one of “modest upside or range-bound action rather than a sharp breakout,” citing mixed broader market conditions as a factor keeping expectations measured. The Base Case: $1.28 to $1.35 The base case projection places XRP just above its current level by month’s end. Grok pointed to the OCC’s final approval of the Ripple National Trust Bank charter as a credibility-strengthening development, while noting it does not directly drive immediate XRP demand. It described the BNY Mellon custody support, Robinhood integration, and Aviva’s tokenized fund activity as producing “gradual effects” rather than near-term price catalysts. Bullish Case: $1.40 and Above If institutional partnerships translate into measurable on-chain activity, Grok expects XRP to trade at a minimum of $1.40. This outcome would depend on a technical breakout above resistance near $1.35 to $1.40, improved broader crypto market sentiment, and additional positive developments following the Swell conference announcements . The AI tool also cited whale accumulation patterns as a supporting factor. If whales choose to scoop up tokens at current prices, the demand could add to the bullish momentum. Bearish and Sideways Case: $1.15 to $1.28 Grok outlined a scenario in which XRP remains flat or retreats modestly. The target range is $1.15-$1.28. Much of the recent infrastructure development centers on RLUSD and custody arrangements rather than generating direct demand for XRP itself. Some in the community have raised concerns about this trend, but Ripple has consistently reassured them that RLUSD will not replace XRP . What to Expect from XRP Grok closed with a standard caution that “crypto prices remain highly volatile and sensitive to macro factors, so actual outcomes can deviate quickly.” The forecast represents one AI model’s probabilistic analysis, not financial advice, and XRP’s trajectory could be significantly different. title: Riot Platforms: The AI Pivot Is Gaining Momentum, But The Timing Isn't Ideal
body: Summary Riot Platforms shifts toward stable energy infrastructure with a 910 MW, $1.8B AI data center deal at Corsicana, Texas. Q3 2026 results show improved mining efficiency, significant BTC sales for $1.5B cash, and a pivot to triple net lease agreements. Financing for Corsicana's $5.5B buildout remains uncertain, with risks from potential leverage and Texas's new political climate threatening data center approvals. I downgrade RIOT from Buy to Hold due to transition risks, macro headwinds, and a preference for more established energy infrastructure providers. Q3 2026: a new deal that expands the energy potential Q3 results of Riot Platforms, Inc. ( RIOT ) show a new deal for 910 MW with a leading AI lab, with an initial agreement value of $28 million, to be distributed over 15 years. This would represent an NOI (net operating income) of approximately $1.8 billion and aligns with the company’s goal of shifting toward a more stable business that doesn’t depend on Bitcoin’s volatility. RIOT doesn’t reveal the identity of the client, but from our previous coverage we know there are already attractive deals with Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. ( AMD ), which in turn, as I explained in this article , has a chip supply deal with Anthropic, PBC ( ANT ), the company that owns Claude and is preparing to go public. The deal is focused on the Corsicana facility in Texas, the company's largest, where it will build capacity for 1 GW. The other two sites, Rockdale and Kentucky, represent the rest of the installed capacity. Rockdale will host AMD, while Kentucky is expected to serve as additional capacity. For now, the operating sites are still dedicated to crypto mining, as I’ll explain later. At this point, the Bitcoin exit management is serving as a beneficial cash reserve to finance the infrastructure buildout. Riot Platforms Of that Corsicana capacity, 910 MW is the critical energy contracted by this leading AI lab. The project is expected to be built in 3 phases, with the goal of making the service operational by July 2028. The projected average annual revenue is $1.8 billion, above the projections I made in previous articles, which were around $1.6 billion in total. Besides the potential of this agreement, the context of high borrowing costs and several market doubts about neocloud leverage force me to review in more detail the financing of these projects. Building this site requires a CAPEX of $5.5 billion. Between 80 and 90% of these resources will be defined through 2 avenues, which are not complementary: either through non-recourse debt, meaning off-balance-sheet debt, which implies extra risk given the current context, or through advance payments from the tenant, with repayment commitments through the rent obtained. RIOT would put up between $500 million and $1.1 billion of its own cash in Path A, or $1.8 billion between cash and debt in Path B. Riot Platforms RIOT has an initial advantage by owning the land and the physical infrastructure, and this is the part of the value chain I like. The tenant brings the chips with their respective servers, which in turn are used to bill its users. But the electrical infrastructure, the energy capacity, and the physical facilities belong to RIOT. I believe this will be an advantage over time in the future development of AI and for any energy needs that arise. But at the same time, commitments of this nature become increasingly difficult to sustain if a large part is based on risky leverage. Since I don’t yet know which financing path RIOT will choose, I’m skeptical. I would prefer it to be through tenant advance payments rather than debt. Anyway, it carries risks, and now I’m factoring in a more complex scenario following Tuesday’s midterm elections. This major announcement by RIOT focuses its energy potential in Corsicana, Texas, a state that the Republican Party has lost, whose governor Greg Abbott has not been opposed to data center construction, as it was part of the national project to drive the country’s technological development. The newly elected governor, Gina Hinojosa, of the Democratic Party, won the election with 53% of the votes , versus 46% for Abbott. This is not something that affects only RIOT, given that 27% of all the GW projected for data centers are concentrated in Texas. According to Reuters , Hinojosa promised to freeze all approvals for new data centers until laws protecting state power grids are passed. The Republican candidate had also slightly shifted his position, but it wasn’t enough to reverse the Democratic victory. In the same Reuters article, other previous polls show hostility toward these sites. “Some 76% of voters nationwide said they opposed the construction of a new data center in their community, according to an NBC and SSRS exit poll. Ahead of the vote, a University of Houston poll ⁠in October ​found that 79% of likely Texas voters supported limits on the number of data centers that can ​be built in the state.” Source: Reuters This political shift, combined with the macroeconomic complications, makes me much more cautious about the developments RIOT is looking to complete in the coming years. Q3: improved efficiency and sound management of BTC, but with accelerated sales RIOT’s proposal is to close as many NNN (triple net lease) deals as possible that guarantee stable billing as an energy infrastructure provider. In previous articles, I explained that this is the segment that interests me most in AI development. That’s why RIOT’s pivot is exactly what I was hoping to see. Part of this transition sent a clear message in the recent earnings report, as the company sold 20,264 BTC so far in 2026, generating $1.5 billion in cash. This allowed it to avoid issuing shares and the dilution that other companies in the sector need to resort to in order to finance themselves. This amount could, for example, immediately finance part of the development of new phases at Corsicana. But for now there is no certainty about how it will be used. It's a good resource. Anyway, perhaps this sale ended up being premature. Basically, I believe the BTC bear cycle could be just beginning. I see several technical signals that make me think we’ll seek new all-time highs. Therefore, cash flow was realized before seeing better BTC prices. Riot still holds 2,418 BTC, representing approximately $200 million. The company has been producing between 1,400 and 1,600 BTC per quarter. In Q3, it produced 1,637 BTC. It keeps improving its margins quarter after quarter, but it doesn't have a reserve like it used to. Besides this, this selloff sends a good message to investors expecting a faster business transition. Ergo, although I would have preferred to wait for higher prices to sell, I appreciate this signal. Besides, RIOT keeps improving its mining efficiency, and on a YoY basis, it lowered its cost per mined BTC from $89,074 to $78,805 (see slide 45 of the 10-Q), including depreciation of its machines. Another key metric to understand mining efficiency is the EH/s record of 44.9 in Q3, up from 36.5 EH/s a year ago. Riot Platforms Q3: a quarter with no net losses, but one that will round off a difficult year The company had revenue of $181 million, a slight increase from the $180 million a year ago. Of this revenue, only $18 million corresponds to the data center segment, while $115 million still depends on BTC. The company showed net earnings of $4 million, compared to losses of $237 million in the previous quarter and nearly $500 million lost in Q1. This is largely due to better revenue generated in the BTC segment. But there were also accounting improvements, both in the value of derivatives (changes in the value of its electricity contracts) and higher depreciation and amortization. This is the case both compared to the previous quarter and to the same quarter a year ago. This also improved its adjusted EBITDA, which came in at $195 million, while in Q2 it was negative $140 million. I usually pay more attention to adjusted EBITDA in these companies because it better reflects the business transition path, while the current billing doesn’t allow you to visualize the future business model. Anyway, although Q3 showed some operating improvements and its EBITDA also improved, the first 9 months of the year still represent a period of losses and high transition costs. So far this year, revenue was $522 million, an increase of 5.7% from the $494 million in the same period the previous year. But net losses are $733 million, versus earnings of $27 million in the same period of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA has been negative so far this year, at $189 million. Riot Platforms The thing is that RIOT still can’t generate cash flow from its current business, and despite having raised cash through the large BTC sale, I think it could now be exposed to financing needs heading into 2027, where billing still can’t show major improvements from its data center revenue. I foresee there will be more losses in 2027, and I expect it will be the last year of operating difficulties before completing the transition to AI hosting. Risks The sector of former BTC miners transforming their business into premium AI hosting has been heavily punished in recent months amid the broad AI selloff. Current price levels suggest we could be near a strong rebound, and from there a possible bullish reversal. RIOT, for example, had its RSI below 30 at the end of October, an oversold indicator that typically anticipates some kind of recovery. As of November 4th, the recent rally brought it to 50 points. The other former crypto miners are in a similar situation, but with a weaker RSI. Basically, the risk of my investment decision is whether the short-term rebounds are strong enough to change market sentiment. My verdict Given this Q3 scenario, I believe RIOT will continue depending on BTC production for both revenue and cash generation. The alternatives of share issuance or taking on debt to advance data center construction represent a risk in my investment outlook. So, I keep reducing my exposure to the weaker segments within the AI investment cycle. Although RIOT has been one of my favorite stocks during 2025 and 2026, because I believe it has significant potential, being positioned in the energy supply chain, the economic, financial, and now electoral conditions represent important obstacles for a strong rebound in the share price. I believe the rise in the share price last Wednesday of up to 12% represented an opportunity for those looking to exit some volatile assets and seek more defensive alternatives. I chose to maintain positions in RIOT peer companies, such as Hut 8 Corp. ( HUT ) and IREN Limited ( IREN ), for their larger capitalization and more ambitious installed capacity projects, where hyperscalers guarantee the construction of their facilities. But I’m keeping a close eye on the sector, and any financial complication in the market could make me change my view. As an added note, both companies are also betting on Texas, which broadens the risks. I still trust in the AI energy value chain, but I continue to prefer more consolidated stocks, oriented toward power grids and larger energy infrastructure providers, whose core business is not directly tied to AI. They are large energy providers, but only a portion of their business is oriented toward the data center boom. My largest positions today are in the utilities Talen Energy Corporation ( TLN ) and TransAlta Corporation ( TAC ). Given the market circumstances and the bearish trend I see in the more fragile links of the AI chain, I am lowering my rating on RIOT from Buy to Hold.
